subject: Heart valve stenosis, including aortic stenosis,
object: when a heart valve does not open fully.
source: NHS website: Heart valve disease
source_quote: Heart valve disease happens when 1 of your heart valves either: does not open fully (called stenosis)

subject: Heart valve disease
object: most common in the aortic or mitral valves, on the left side of the heart, though it can affect any of the 4 heart valves.
source: NHS website: Heart valve disease
source_quote: It can affect any of your 4 heart valves, but it's most common in the aortic or mitral valves, on the left side of your heart.

subject: Calcific aortic stenosis
object: the most common valve disease in developed countries, in which valves thicken and stiffen, and in some cases nodular deposits form, limiting valve function.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is the most common valve disease in developed countries (,), in which valves thicken and stiffen, and in some cases nodular deposits form, limiting valve function.

subject: Aortic stenosis
object: the most frequent valvular heart disease worldwide, expected to increase in prevalence due to the ageing population.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Aortic stenosis (AS) is the most frequent valvular heart disease (VHD) worldwide, expected to increase in prevalence due to the aging population.

subject: Calcific aortic stenosis
object: a progressive disease that advances with age, affecting about 0.2% of people aged 50 to 59 and increasing to 9.8% of those aged 80 to 89.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Calcific AS is a progressive disease that advances with age (,), affecting ~0.2% of people 50–59 years of age and increasing to 9.8% for 80–89 years (,).

subject: Statistical modelling of severe aortic stenosis
object: an incidence of 4% to 7% per year among people aged 65 or over.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Statistical modeling has estimated an incidence rate of severe AS ranging from 4% to 7% per year among people ≥65 years of age .

subject: Calcific degeneration
object: by far the most common cause of aortic valve stenosis, with an estimated prevalence of 0.4% in the general population and 1.7% in people over 65 in developed countries.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Calcific degeneration, by far, is the most common cause of aortic valve stenosis and has an estimated prevalence of 0.4% in the general population and 1.7% in the population >65 years of age, in developed countries .

subject: In calcific aortic stenosis, whether the underlying valve is tricuspid or bicuspid
object: age, as bicuspid valves are much more frequent in younger patients.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Firstly, the prevalence of tricuspid or bicuspid valves, as the underlying anatomy of calcific AS, relies on age , as bicuspid valves are much more frequent in younger patients.

subject: Bicuspid aortic valve
object: a prevalence of between 0.5% and 1%, and in about 75% of cases the fusion is between the right and left coronary cusps.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: The prevalence of bicuspid aortic valve ranges between 0.5% and 1% and different fusion patterns are described: in about 75% of cases, the fusion is between the right and the left coronary cusps, in about 14% of cases is between the right and non-coronary cusps, while the fusion between the left and non-coronary cusps or a bicuspid valve with two same-size cusps are less-common findings (Figure 2).

subject: In aortic stenosis, calcification along the edges of the cusps leading to commissural fusion, with a triangular systolic orifice,
object: rheumatic heart disease as the cause.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Conversely, aortic valve calcification located along the edges of the cusps leading to commissural fusion, with a characteristic triangular systolic orifice, is suggestive of rheumatic heart disease (RHD) as the etiologic cause of AS.

subject: Rheumatic heart disease, a cause of aortic stenosis,
object: about 34 million people worldwide, resulting in 340,000 deaths a year, although rheumatic disease is decreasing in industrialised countries; rheumatic disease is caused by an untreated throat infection with group A Streptococcus.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Although the prevalence of rheumatic disease, which is an immune-mediated multisystem inflammatory disease caused by an untreated throat infection with group A Streptococcus, is decreasing in industrialized countries, about 34 million people worldwide are affected by RHD, resulting in 340,000 deaths and 10 million disability-adjusted life-years lost per year .

subject: Congenital aortic stenosis
object: rarely diagnosed in adults, as it is usually discovered in newborns or at a young age.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: The diagnosis of congenital AS is rare in adult patients as this defect is usually discovered early in the neonatal or young ages .

subject: Old age, male sex, diabetes, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol and smoking
object: the risk of aortic valve calcification, which leads to calcific aortic stenosis.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: For years, calcification was thought to be a passive degenerative process in which calcium accumulates on leaflets (, –), where old age, male gender, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, chronic renal disease, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and smoking are known to increase the risk for AV calcification ().

subject: Plasma lipoprotein (a)
object: an independent risk factor for aortic stenosis, identified through genome-wide association studies.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Plasma lipoprotein (a) is an independent risk factor of AS identified through genome-wide association studies (–).

subject: Degenerative calcific aortic stenosis
object: an active process: damage to the valve lining, lipid build-up and inflammation lead to valve fibrosis and thickening that over time evolve into severe valve calcification.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Degenerative calcific AS is an active process characterized by the disruption of the aortic valvular endothelium with endothelial dysfunction, lipid accumulation, and infiltration of lymphocytes and macrophages that release pro-inflammatory molecules; they recruit fibroblasts and activate osteoblasts, leading to valve fibrosis, progressive thickening, that, over time, evolves into severe valve calcification .

subject: In aortic stenosis, valve calcification
object: restricted leaflet movement, a smaller valve area and obstruction to flow.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Therefore, valve calcification leads to restriction of leaflets mobility, valve area reduction, and flow obstruction.

subject: Calcification of the aortic valve
object: a complex process involving mechanobiology, molecular signalling, tissue remodelling and inflammation, rather than passive calcium build-up.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Now, it is understood that calcification is a complex process involving mechanobiology, molecular signaling, tissue remodeling, and inflammation as the AV opens and closes billions of times during a lifetime.

subject: Aortic stenosis
object: pressure overload in the left ventricle which, untreated, can lead to hypertrophy and, long term, to systolic failure and congestive heart failure.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Pressure overload can occur in the left ventricle, and when left untreated, this can lead to hypertrophy (). Presence of long-term pressure overload can even eventually lead to systolic failure and congestive heart failure.

subject: Severe aortic stenosis
object: chronic pressure overload that leads to left ventricular hypertrophy, which is compensatory early on but increases the heart muscle's oxygen demand without a matching increase in its capillary network.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Severe AS is associated with chronic pressure overload that causes an increase in LV wall stress and leads to a hypertrophic response of the cardiomyocytes. Although effective in an early stage, this compensatory effect increases myocardial oxygen demand, in the absence of a balanced increase in the coronary capillary network.

subject: In aortic stenosis, left ventricular hypertrophy
object: heart muscle cell degeneration, death and fibrosis, and when wall stress exceeds the compensating mechanism, the left ventricle's pumping declines.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: This will progressively lead to myocyte degeneration, death, and fibrosis . When wall stress exceeds the compensating mechanism, LV contractile function declines .

subject: Cardiac damage in aortic stenosis
object: the aortic valve: it affects the whole cardiovascular system and can significantly alter the other heart chambers.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Cardiac damage in AS is not limited to the aortic valve but is a disease affecting the entire cardiovascular system that can be characterized by significant alteration of the other cardiac chambers.

subject: In aortic stenosis, raised left atrial pressure
relation: is transmitted back through the lungs
object: leading to right heart remodelling and dysfunction; echo signs of pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular dysfunction are found in about 30% and 25% of patients.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Moreover, the increased left atrial pressure is retrogradely transmitted through the pulmonary vasculature, leading to right heart remodeling and dysfunction . In AS patients, echocardiographic markers of pulmonary hypertension (PH) and right ventricle (RV) systolic dysfunction have a prevalence of about 30 and 25%, respectively .

subject: Patients with severe aortic stenosis
object: a heart murmur, chest pain, shortness of breath, tiredness and fainting (syncope).
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Severe AS can result in serious problems. Patients can experience heart murmur, chest pain, shortness of breath, fatigue and syncope.

subject: Symptoms of heart valve disease, such as aortic stenosis,
object: shortness of breath, feeling tired or weak, feeling dizzy, palpitations, swollen ankles and feet, and chest pain or discomfort.
source: NHS website: Heart valve disease
source_quote: Symptoms of heart valve disease can include: shortness of breath feeling tired or weak feeling dizzy heart palpitations, where you suddenly feel your heart beating irregularly or faster than usual swollen ankles and feet chest pain or discomfort

subject: Heart valve disease, such as aortic stenosis,
object: no symptoms, and is sometimes found by chance when a doctor hears a heart murmur.
source: NHS website: Heart valve disease
source_quote: Some people do not have any symptoms. Sometimes it's found by chance if a doctor hears an unusual sound (a heart murmur) when they listen to your chest.

subject: People with severe aortic stenosis
object: their daily activities to avoid symptoms such as breathlessness, so they can be mistakenly classed as having no symptoms.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: However, patients affected by severe AS often limit their daily activities to avoid symptoms occurrence, such as dyspnea, thus they can be mistakenly classified as asymptomatic.

subject: Echocardiography
object: the most important diagnostic tool in assessing aortic stenosis.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Echocardiography represents the most important diagnostic tool in the evaluation of aortic stenosis.

subject: Tests for heart valve disease, such as aortic stenosis,
object: an ultrasound scan of the heart (echocardiogram), a chest X-ray and an ECG.
source: NHS website: Heart valve disease
source_quote: Tests you may have include: an ultrasound scan of your heart (echocardiogram) an X-ray of your chest an electrocardiogram (ECG), where sensors are put on your chest to check your heart

subject: Echocardiography in aortic stenosis
object: looking at the valve in parasternal long- and short-axis views to identify the number, movement, thickness and calcification of the cusps and to find the cause.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: The first echocardiographic approach in the evaluation of AS begins with the characterization of aortic valve morphology by transthoracic parasternal long- and short-axis views, in order to identify the number, mobility, thickness, and calcification of the cusps and to evaluate the etiology .

subject: Aortic stenosis severity
object: the flow velocity through the valve, the valve opening area and the pressure gradient across the valve.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Aortic stenosis severity can be assessed based on valve flow velocity, valve orifice area, and the pressure gradient across the valve (,).

subject: The first measurement to make when looking for aortic stenosis
object: the aortic jet velocity, measured with continuous-wave Doppler.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: The first hemodynamic parameter that needs to be evaluated when searching for AS is the aortic jet velocity (Table 1) measured with continuous-wave (CW) Doppler .

subject: When measuring aortic stenosis
object: should always be used to find the highest velocity.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Multiple acoustic windows should always be used to determine the highest velocity .

subject: Ignoring non-apical windows when measuring aortic stenosis
object: misclassifying the aortic stenosis in up to 23% of patients.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: They proved that neglecting non-apical windows results in the misclassification of AS in up to 23% of patients .

subject: In aortic stenosis, the mean gradient across the valve
object: it is the average gradient during the whole of systole and correlates better than the peak gradient with the peak-to-peak gradient at cardiac catheterisation.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Conversely, the mean gradient, which represents the average gradient during the entire systole, has been shown to better correlate with the peak-to-peak gradient obtained during cardiac catheterization, and should always be measured.

subject: In aortic stenosis, aortic valve area
object: particularly with very low or very high flow, because unlike velocity and gradient it varies less with cardiac output.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Differently from flow velocity and pressure gradients that vary with cardiac output (Table 1), AVA should always be calculated, particularly in patients with very low or very high flow rates, since it has higher stability over a range of hemodynamic states .

subject: Mild aortic stenosis
object: a valve area over 1.5 cm², a peak velocity between 2.6 and 2.9 m/s and a mean gradient below 20 mmHg.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: a valve area >1.5 cm 2, a peak velocity between 2.6 and 2.9 m/s, a mean gradient <20 mmHg define a mild stenosis;

subject: Moderate aortic stenosis
object: a valve area between 1.5 and 1 cm², a peak velocity between 3 and 4 m/s, or a mean gradient between 20 and 40 mmHg.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: a valve area between 1.5 and 1 cm 2, a peak velocity between 3 and 4 m/s, or a mean gradient between 20 and 40 mmHg define a moderate stenosis;

subject: Severe aortic stenosis
object: a peak velocity of 4 m/s or more, a mean gradient of 40 mmHg or more and a valve area of 1 cm² or less, or an indexed valve area of 0.6 cm²/m² or less.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: a peak velocity ≥ 4 m/s, a mean gradient ≥ 40 mmHg and an AVA ≤ 1 cm 2, or an indexed (to body surface area) AVA (AVAi) ≤ 0.6 cm 2 /m 2 are the criteria proposed by current guidelines to identify severe stenosis.

subject: The criteria for grading aortic stenosis
object: consistent, and the proportion of patients with discordant measurements is not negligible.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Nonetheless, these criteria are not always consistent and the proportion of patients with discordant parameters is not negligible .

subject: Almost 30 to 40% of patients with an aortic valve area of 1 cm² or less
object: a mean gradient below 40 mmHg (low-gradient aortic stenosis).
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Almost 30–40% of patients with AVA ≤ 1 cm 2 have a mean gradient < 40 mmHg; when the above-mentioned causes are excluded, an accurate evaluation of SV indexed (SVi) and LV ejection fraction (LVEF) is mandatory in order to discriminate between three forms of low-gradient severe AS (Figure 5) :

subject: Classical low-flow low-gradient aortic stenosis
object: a mean gradient below 40 mmHg, stroke volume index of 35 mL/m² or less and ejection fraction below 50%, and is found in 5 to 10% of aortic stenosis cases.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Classical low-flow low-gradient (cLFLG) AS, characterized by mean aortic transvalvular pressure gradient < 40 mmHg, SVi ≤ 35 mL/m 2 and LVEF < 50%, and is detected in 5–10% of the AS cases;

subject: Paradoxical low-flow low-gradient aortic stenosis
object: a mean gradient below 40 mmHg, stroke volume index of 35 mL/m² or less and ejection fraction of 50% or more, and mostly affects women with small ventricles with concentric remodelling.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Paradoxical low-flow low-gradient (pLFLG) AS, characterized by mean aortic transvalvular pressure gradient < 40 mmHg, SVi ≤ 35 mL/m 2 and LVEF ≥ 50%. In the vast majority, this type of AS affects women with small and concentric remodeled ventricles, that are responsible for the low flow state.

subject: In low-flow low-gradient severe aortic stenosis, dobutamine stress echocardiography
object: true severe aortic stenosis from pseudo-severe aortic stenosis, where a weak left ventricle (for example after a heart attack) cannot fully open a valve that is only mildly or moderately narrowed.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: In the presence of LFLG severe AS, dobutamine stress-echocardiography (DSE) is crucial in order to distinguish between true severe AS and what is called pseudo-severe AS . As a matter of fact, an effective orifice area ≤ 1 cm 2 and an LVEF < 50% may depend either on a truly stenotic valve or on LV dysfunction: prior myocardial infarction, for example, can cause the inability of the LV to completely open aortic valve cusps, despite the presence of a merely mildly or moderately stenotic valve (pseudo-severe AS).

subject: Exercise stress echocardiography in severe aortic stenosis without reported symptoms
object: to unmask symptoms or abnormal blood pressure responses; exercise testing is contraindicated in symptomatic severe aortic stenosis.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Symptomatic severe AS represents a class I indication for AVR, with no need for further evaluation ; exercise testing is contraindicated in this population. Therefore, exercise stress echocardiography (ESE) is recommended to unmask symptoms or abnormal blood pressure responses in this population, in order to obtain a more punctual risk stratification.

subject: Calcific aortic stenosis
object: computed tomography, which gives a high-resolution assessment of calcification and accurate measurement of leaflet anatomy and annulus geometry.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Calcific AS can be additionally assessed by computed tomography (CT) which provides high-resolution assessment of calcification, and enables accurate measurement of leaflet anatomy and annulus geometry.

subject: In aortic stenosis with discordant echo measurements, ECG-gated CT
object: aortic valve calcification by the Agatston method; a score above 1300 AU in women or 2000 AU in men should be considered severe.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: In particular, in the presence of discordant echocardiographic markers of AS, electrocardiogram-gated CT scans allow the measurement of aortic valve calcification with the use of the Agatston method: an aortic valve calcification score higher than 1300 AU in women or 2000 AU in men should be considered severe .

subject: In aortic stenosis, cardiac catheterisation
object: in rare cases where Doppler echocardiography measurements disagree, to measure pressure directly.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: In rare cases when there are discrepancies in Doppler echocardiography measurements, cardiac catheterization is used to obtain a more accurate measurement of pressure directly from the blood vessel.

subject: In aortic stenosis, colour and pulsed-wave Doppler, with assessment of the outflow tract and ascending aorta,
object: obstruction at the valve from obstruction above or below it.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Furthermore, in order to better understand the nature and the localization of the stenosis, the Color Doppler and the pulsed-wave (PW) Doppler methods can precisely define the site of increased velocity and, together with the anatomical evaluation of the left ventricle outflow tract (LVOT) and the ascending aorta, they allow to discriminate between valvular, supra- or sub-valvular obstructions.

subject: Dynamic obstruction below the aortic valve, often linked to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy,
object: in severity during the cardiac cycle and is greatest in mid-to-late systole, with a late peak in the velocity curve.
source: Article: Manzo R, Ilardi F, Nappa D et al. Echocardiographic Evaluation of Aortic Stenosis: A Comprehensive Review. Diagnostics 2023
source_quote: Dynamic obstruction, often linked to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, refers to a form that changes in severity during the cardiac cycle and prevails during mid-to-late systole with a late peak in the velocity curve .

subject: In calcific aortic stenosis, medicines
object: to slow the progression of the disease or reverse calcification.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: To date, pharmacotherapy has not been shown to slow down the progression of the disease, or to reverse the calcification process ().

subject: In calcific aortic stenosis, lowering LDL cholesterol with statins
object: the progression of the disease, even when given at early stages of calcification.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Despite the link of LDL with calcification, studies have found that LDL suppression or lipid-lowering therapy with statins (anti-inflammatory and antioxidant agents) do not slow down the progression of disease even when given at early stages of calcification (–).

subject: At late stages of calcific aortic stenosis
object: valve repair or replacement, as no therapies can manage the progression of calcification.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: At late stages of calcific AS, no therapies can manage the progression of calcification and the only effective treatment is valve repair or replacement ().

subject: Mild heart valve disease, such as mild aortic stenosis, without symptoms
object: treatment, but there are usually regular check-ups to see if it is getting worse.
source: NHS website: Heart valve disease
source_quote: If you have mild heart valve disease and you do not have any symptoms, you may not need treatment. You'll usually have regular check-ups to see if your condition is getting worse.

subject: Surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR)
object: the most common treatment for severe calcific aortic stenosis: open-heart surgery that replaces the valve with a mechanical or bioprosthetic valve after the calcified leaflets are removed.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) has become the most common treatment for severe calcific aortic stenosis in which patients undergo an open-heart surgery to replace their aortic valve with a mechanical or a bioprosthetic valve; in this procedure calcified native leaflets are cut and removed.

subject: Surgical aortic valve replacement for aortic stenosis
object: symptoms and survival, but mechanical valves carry a risk of thrombosis that can cause a stroke or heart attack, and bioprosthetic valves often calcify over time.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: SAVR improves symptoms and survival, but it comes with risks of thrombosis in mechanical valves that can cause stroke or heart attack, or in the case of bioprosthetic valves, durability is an issue with these valves often calcifying over time ().

subject: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR or TAVI) for aortic stenosis
object: a less invasive technique in which a stented valve is delivered through a catheter and expanded to replace the calcified native valve.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: TAVR is a less invasive technology in which a stented valve is delivered to the location of native valve through a catheter and is expanded to replace the calcified native aortic valve and leaflets.

subject: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement for aortic stenosis
object: an alternative for older patients who were inoperable or at high surgical risk, but is now common practice for lower-risk patients, with equal or better outcomes than surgery.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Initially, in older patients who are inoperable or are at high risk for surgery, transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) was an alternative option. However, this option is now common practice for lower risk patients, as the devices and procedures have advanced with equal to improved outcomes compared to SAVR (,).

subject: TAVR and SAVR for aortic stenosis
object: in trials in high-, intermediate- and low-risk patients (PARTNER 1, 2 and 3).
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: With 3 trials (PARTNER 1, 2, and 3), TAVR vs. SAVR have been studied in high-, intermediate-, and low-risk patients.

subject: In high-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis (PARTNER 1), TAVR compared with SAVR
object: more vascular complications at 1 month and more major strokes at 1 year, while major bleeding was more frequent after surgery.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: However, vascular complications were significantly higher in the transcatheter group at 1-month (11% TAVR vs. 3.2% SAVR). The rate of major strokes at 1-year were more than twice as high in the transcatheter group (5.1% TAVR vs. 2.4% SAVR). Meanwhile, major bleeding was more frequent in the surgical group (19.5% SAVR vs. 9.3% TAVR) ().

subject: In severe aortic stenosis
object: depends on the development of symptoms once the valve is classed as severe.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Timing of intervention depends on the development of clinical symptoms once the valve is classified as severe.

subject: Mechanical heart valves, used to replace a stenosed aortic valve,
object: highly durable, lasting up to 25 years without major complications, but have a high risk of thrombosis; their durability makes them more suitable for patients under 50.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: MHVs are highly durable when compared with other artificial heart valves; they can last up to 25 years in patients without major complications, but they have high risk of thrombosis (). High durability makes these valves more suitable for patients younger than age 50, as MHVs have a lower risk of reoperation ().

subject: Patients with mechanical heart valves
object: lifelong anticoagulants to prevent thrombosis and thromboembolism, but these drugs increase the risk of bleeding, stroke, systemic embolism, cardiac tamponade and death.

source_quote: Patients treated with mechanical valves need a lifelong anticoagulant drug therapy to prevent thrombosis and thromboembolism (); however these drugs increase the risk of bleeding, stroke, systemic embolism, cardiac tamponade and death ().

subject: Bioprosthetic heart valves
object: pig or cow pericardium, are less thrombotic and need only short-term anticoagulation after surgery, but often need reoperation because of deterioration and calcification, lasting only about 15 years on average.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Bioprosthetic heart valves (BHV) are made of porcine or bovine pericardium. They have the advantage of being less thrombotic, requiring only short-term anticoagulation after surgery. The main disadvantage of BHVs is that they often require reoperation due to structural valve deterioration and calcification, making the average BHV lifetime only ~15 years.

subject: Balloon aortic valvuloplasty for aortic stenosis
object: a catheter technique that widens the narrowed valve by inflating a balloon in it, passed through the femoral artery.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) is a catheter-based technique that dilates native valve's narrowed opening by delivering and inflating a balloon at the site of stenosed valve through femoral artery ().

subject: Balloon aortic valvuloplasty in adults with aortic stenosis
object: long-term improvement, as the valve can narrow again, so it is a temporary option and a bridge to SAVR or TAVR for high-risk patients needing urgent intervention.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: BAV procedures do not provide long term improvements in adults, as the dilated valve can become restenosed; therefore, BAV is a temporary improvement option and a bridge to SAVR or TAVR for patients who are at high risk and need an urgent intervention ().

subject: Balloon aortic valvuloplasty
object: as palliation in terminal patients with under a year to live, to improve quality of life in the short term.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Utilization of BAV is also practiced as a palliative treatment option in terminal patients with <1-year life expectancy to improve quality of life in the short term, often seen in the hospice population.

subject: Possible complications of heart valve disease, such as aortic stenosis,
object: heart failure, atrial fibrillation, stroke and endocarditis.
source: NHS website: Heart valve disease
source_quote: Possible complications of heart valve disease include: heart failure, where your heart cannot pump blood properly atrial fibrillation, where your heart beats irregularly and faster than normal a stroke endocarditis, a serious condition where your heart becomes infected

subject: Some of the most frequent complications of TAVR for aortic stenosis
object: valve malpositioning, coronary obstruction, paravalvular leak, leaflet damage from crimping, thrombosis, conduction abnormalities and prosthesis-patient mismatch.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Some of the most frequent complications occurring with TAVR procedures are TAV malpositioning, coronary obstruction, paravalvular leak, crimped-induced leaflet damage, thrombosis, conduction abnormalities, and prosthetic-patient mismatch ().

subject: Conduction abnormalities after TAVR for aortic stenosis
object: tissue damage during valve deployment, and balloon-expandable valves generally need pacemakers less often than self-expanding valves.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Conduction abnormalities can be caused by tissue damage during valve deployment. In general, balloon-expandable valves have lower rates of pacemaker requirements compared to self-expandable TAVs.

subject: Coronary obstruction
object: a rare (under 1% of patients) but life-threatening complication of TAVR for aortic stenosis.
source: Article: Zebhi B, Lazkani M, Bark D. Calcific Aortic Stenosis—A Review on Acquired Mechanisms of the Disease and Treatments. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine 2021
source_quote: Coronary obstruction is a rare consequence of TAVR that occurs during the procedure in <1% of patients, but it is life-threatening (,,) as it restricts blood flow circulation in coronary arteries.

subject: Aortic stenosis

source_quote: It can lead to gastrointestinal, skin, and mucosal bleeding, which may, in-part, be attributed to acquired von Willebrand syndrome (AVWS) also known as Heydes Syndrome (–). It appears as though the AVWS stems from turbulence that can occur in an aortic stenosis, whereas it is often alleviated once a diseased valve is replaced, eliminating pathological flow (, –).
